system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar stress: energy shocks, financial strain, tech rivalry, and regional wars
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system driven by intersecting processes: Middle East conflict and energy-market disruptions, renewed great-power competition in technology and regional security (notably around Taiwan and Ukraine), and acute financial-market stress amplified by sovereign debt strains in Europe. Domestic political instability (protests, riots) and accelerating climate risks increase feedbacks across markets, supply chains and alliance politics, producing high volatility and policy uncertainty worldwide.
system_description.scope: Interstate security crises (Middle East, Ukraine, Taiwan), major-power strategic competition (US, China, Russia, EU), global energy supply and markets, international financial and sovereign-bond markets, strategic technology and supply chains (AI, semiconductors, satellite services), climate-driven risks and transnational political unrest.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-ecological-economic-political system (the integrated global civilization system encompassing climate, economies, international politics and transnational flows).
adjacent_subsystems: Global Energy Markets and Maritime Security

variables.name: Middle East Gulf escalation
variables.description: Iran, Saudi Arabia, Houthi forces and Israel are engaged in an expanding military and proxy escalation that is shifting regional security dynamics and threatening Gulf energy flows.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and diplomacy
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in high‑intensity conflict even as episodic diplomacy and third‑party envoys attempt to reshape battlefield dynamics and potential ceasefire terms.

variables.name: US–China tech and supply rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting leadership in semiconductors, AI, cleantech and strategic materials, reshaping supply chains, investment rules and trade barriers.

variables.name: Eurozone sovereign bond stress
variables.description: Eurozone governments and investors, with acute strains in France and other vulnerable issuers, are witnessing a sharp repricing of sovereign risk that is altering capital flows, monetary space and financial stability.

variables.name: Turkey-led regional defence realignment
variables.description: Turkey, together with partners such as Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia, is forging new defence and diplomatic pacts that are shifting regional security alignments and diversifying non‑Western partnerships.
